newsitem.title: THAILAND: Amnuay sees no reason for bank governor to resign.
newsitem.headline: Amnuay sees no reason for bank governor to resign.

text.p: Thai Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan said on Thursday that he saw no reason for central bank governor Rerngchai Marakanond to resign over a government decision to suspend his deputy who handled a bungled court case against executives of Bangkok Bank of Commerce Plc.
Amnuay told reporters: "I would like to make it clear that ... there is no reason for the governor to resign."

The minister said although the suspension of deputy central bank governor Jaroong Nookhwun and two other senior officials may have demoralised their colleagues, he was not aware that some of them planned to stage a protest rally.
Some witnesses at the central bank said some employees had arrived for work dressed in black as a sign of protest against the suspension of their three colleagues.
Amnuay had recently denied rumours that he himself might resign over reported criticism of his recent economic and monetary policies by some cabinet members.

On Thursday, he reiterated his stand. "Such rumours are futile and would not go far," he said. "I would like to make it clear that I am still in charge. These rumours always surface to shake the market."

Deputy governor Jaroong was suspended and put on a one-month disciplinary review on Wednesday in a follow-up to a prosecution decision to drop a civil court case against former top executives of Bangkok Bank of Commerce. They had been charged with Thai Banking Act violations.
Prosecutors were forced to drop the case against former bank president Krirkkiat Jaleechan and his aides because a one-year statute of limitations expired last month.
The Thai baht, which fell early on the rumour, recovered after the rumour was quashed by the central bank.
The currency steadided to be quoted at at 25.948/953 at 0547 GMT after touching a low of 25.965 earlier in the day.
The stock market was mostly unaffected by the rumour.
